preamble: Before being entered in the grid the solutions to twelve clues need three or more of their letterschanged to 19 22 alternatives. All resulting words are real.

clue.text: Third person assumes fitting rank

indicators.note: to assume is to take on or put on, so the third person takes the word for fitting inside him

parts.note: Cain was the third person in Genesis, after Adam and Eve
apt means fitting or suitable

explanation.surface: A grammatical third person taking on a suitable military rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Third person' looks grammatical, but it is Cain, the third human in the Bible. CAPTAIN keys the same phone buttons as ABSTAIN, which is entered.
explanation.definitionFit: A captain is a military or naval officer's grade, so the word names a rank.

clue.text: Stomach upset at lunchtime — working, for a change

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down, so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: tum is an informal word for stomach
taken as written
one o'clock is lunchtime, and one is I
on means working, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: Someone with an upset stomach at lunch at the office, for once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stomach upset' looks like a medical complaint, but it turns the word round. On a phone keypad MUTATION shares keys with OTTAVINO, a piccolo, which is entered.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutation is an alteration in form, most often in genes, so it is a change.

clue.text: Leave girl and monitor lizard

parts.note: to go is to leave
Anna is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A parent telling a child to drop the girl and keep watch over the lizard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monitor' looks like a verb, to watch; it is a kind of lizard. GOANNA and HOBNOB use the same phone keys, and HOBNOB is entered.
explanation.definitionFit: Goanna is the Australian name for any monitor, the large lizards of the genus Varanus.

clue.text: Singer welcomes 1 after 6 dropping by

indicators.note: the singer's piece follows the roman numeral

parts.note: the number six as a roman numeral

indicators.note: to welcome a guest is to take them in, so the singer's name holds the number

parts.note: Sting is the stage name of the former Police singer
one as a roman numeral

explanation.surface: A star singer greeting a fan who calls round after six.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1 and 6 look like cross-references to other clues but are roman numerals. VISITING and THRIVING share phone keys, and THRIVING is entered.
explanation.definitionFit: Visiting means calling on someone briefly, which is dropping by.

clue.text: Outlaw delivers one better than 3 NT?

indicators.note: to deliver a speech is to say it, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: in bridge the bid above three no-trumps is at the four level, so it is a four bid

explanation.surface: A bridge cheat dealing the next bid up from three no-trumps.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge bids rise from one to seven, so after three no-trumps the next call is a four bid. FORBID and ENRAGE share phone keys, and ENRAGE is entered.
explanation.definitionFit: To outlaw something is to ban it by law, so to prohibit it.

clue.text: Former Asian PM divorced husband by note for stud

indicators.note: a divorced husband is parted from the family, so his letter is split off from the name

parts.note: Benazir Bhutto, twice prime minister of Pakistan
N is short for note, as in a banknote

explanation.surface: A gossip item about a Pakistani politician dumping her husband for a younger stallion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stud' looks like a man for the PM's next affair, but it is a fastener on a shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a small fastener pushed through holes in a shirt, much like a button.

clue.text: Calls for strong acids?

definitions.meaning: rings someone on the telephone, a plain verb
strong acids sit at the very bottom of the acidity scale, so they are the ones measuring 1 on it

explanation.surface: A chemist ordering highly corrosive reagents.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as PH ONES: strong acids are the substances with a pH of one.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring someone up on the telephone is to make a call to them.

clue.text: Suddenly, even around ten, lady forgets today's date

indicators.note: the even letters are the second, fourth, sixth and eighth of these words

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of the two words run together

indicators.note: to forget something is to leave it out, so these letters drop from the word

parts.note: taken as written
dates now are AD, anno domini

explanation.surface: A woman abruptly forgets she has a date tonight at ten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even' looks like an adverb but asks for the even letters. RUDELY and STEELY share phone keys, and STEELY is entered.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudely can mean abruptly and without warning, as when someone is rudely awakened.

clue.text: Lots and lots of money? I will get a number of notes

indicators.note: to get here is to become something else, so these letters are reformed

parts.note: the contraction I'll
six is a number, the one the letters need
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lottery winner dreaming of being paid in banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: The number is left for the solver to choose; only six supplies the right letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A sextillion is a thousand million million million, so sextillions of pounds is a vast fortune.

clue.text: Small vehicle race

parts.note: a train is a vehicle that runs on rails

explanation.surface: A soapbox derby or similar contest for tiny carts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Race' reads as a contest, but here it is a breed or lineage.
explanation.definitionFit: A strain is a breed or line of descent within a species, which is one sense of race.

clue.text: Key exercise removes hair

parts.note: E is a musical key
Pilates is a system of body-conditioning exercises

explanation.surface: An essential workout that somehow leaves you bald.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' looks like an adjective meaning important; it is a musical key.
explanation.definitionFit: To epilate is to take out body hair by the roots, as waxing or plucking does.

clue.text: At home I'm spinning a dress

indicators.note: something spinning is turned right round, so these words are read in the opposite order

parts.note: being in means being at home
taken as written, the contraction for I am

explanation.surface: Someone twirling in front of the mirror at home to show off an outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A mini is a short skirt or dress, the miniskirt's cousin, worn well above the knee.

clue.text: Artist born with excessive diamonds rejecting 75% of will

parts.note: OTT stands for over the top
ice is slang for diamonds

indicators.note: rejecting sends the letters back the way they came, so they are read backwards
three letters out of four is 75 per cent, so one letter of the four-letter word is lost

parts.note: taken as written, the four-letter word

explanation.surface: A painter with an over-the-top jewel habit who has been cut out of a will.
explanation.walkthrough: The word loses its first letter, leaving three of four, and those three are read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandro Botticelli was the Florentine Renaissance painter of The Birth of Venus.

clue.text: Cheer up birds, it's digital entertainment!

parts.note: to console someone is to comfort and cheer them
game is the collective term for birds shot for sport, such as grouse and pheasant

explanation.surface: An exclamation that birdsong is now an app you can download.
explanation.definitionFit: A console game is a video game played on a home machine such as a PlayStation, so it is electronic amusement.

clue.text: Silence before one's final bet, with Greek leader playing for time

parts.note: st is an interjection asking for quiet
going all in is staking everything, the last bet one can make

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A poker player goes quiet before pushing in all his chips, while a Greek opponent stalls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing for time' looks like part of the poker scene, a slow player. STALLING shares phone keys with SUCKLING, which is entered.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalling is delaying on purpose to gain time, which is playing for time.

clue.text: Unorthodox mother, Queen Victoria embraces king

parts.note: ma is a child's word for mother

indicators.note: something embracing another holds it within, so the short name wraps around the queen

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Queen Victoria as an eccentric mother hugging her king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen Victoria' looks like one person; the words split into two pieces. MAVERICK shares phone keys with MATERIAL, which is entered.
explanation.definitionFit: A maverick is an independent person who goes against convention, so maverick as an adjective means unconventional.

clue.text: Defend American then lock up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: An instruction to protect the American, then jail him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock up' looks like the definition, to imprison; it is the hair and the turnaround. ASSERT shares phone keys with ARREST, which is entered.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert one's rights is to stand up for and maintain them, which is to defend them.

clue.text: Former wife's suggestion about daughter: send to Coventry?

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse, and the possessive just links

indicators.note: the hint goes around the daughter, enclosing her

parts.note: a clue is a hint or suggestion

explanation.surface: An ex-wife proposes the daughter be shunned.
explanation.walkthrough: To send someone to Coventry is a British idiom for refusing to speak to them. EXCLUDE shares phone keys with EXALTED, which is entered.
explanation.definitionFit: Excluding someone shuts them out of the group, as ostracising does.

clue.text: Anticipating pierced hysterics over ITV comic

indicators.note: words thrown into hysterics are in a wild jumble, so these letters are rearranged
comic means funny or absurd, telling the solver to play about with these letters too
in an across clue, over puts the first piece before the second

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be jumbled
taken as written: ITV is a British commercial television channel

explanation.surface: A TV comedian is being stabbed by hysterical fans, or so a tabloid headline would put it.
explanation.walkthrough: With 22 this gives the theme: predictive text on old phone keypads, where one key sequence spells several words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something predictive forecasts what is coming, so it is looking ahead to events.

clue.text: Stood in awe of The Listener under fine editor

indicators.note: in a down clue, the listener sits below the letter for fine

parts.note: an ear is what listens

explanation.surface: A writer cowering before a fine-wielding editor of The Listener magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Listener was a BBC magazine and is now a famous Times crossword series. FEARED shares phone keys with DECREE, which is entered.
explanation.definitionFit: To fear someone can mean to revere them, as in God-fearing, so to stand in awe.

clue.text: Best agent promoted by top club

indicators.note: by puts the second piece next to the first
promoted means moved up, and in a down clue the word reads upwards

parts.note: a Fed is a US federal agent

indicators.note: to top is to cut off the head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: to club someone is to beat them

explanation.surface: A star agent signed by a top football club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' looks like an adjective but is a verb, to beat. DEFEAT shares phone keys with EFFECT, which is entered.
explanation.definitionFit: To best an opponent is to beat or overcome them.

clue.text: Reading from New Testament extract

indicators.note: taken from the run of letters, so the answer sits inside them

parts.note: NT is the standard abbreviation for the New Testament, placed before the word extract

explanation.surface: A lesson read aloud in church from the Gospels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extract' looks like the definition, a passage, but its letters hold the answer once NT stands in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A reading is a passage or text read out, as in a church service.

clue.text: Provisionally arrange course of medicine with iodine left out

indicators.note: left out means dropped, so these two letters are removed

parts.note: penicillin is the antibiotic often prescribed as a course

explanation.surface: A doctor booking a provisional prescription of antibiotics minus one ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: I is the chemical symbol for iodine.
explanation.definitionFit: To pencil something in is to schedule it tentatively, in erasable pencil rather than ink.

clue.text: Feel angry about sport being used for punishment?

indicators.note: the reworked letters go round the sport, enclosing it
angry words are worked up and agitated, so these letters are stirred about

parts.note: taken as written
RU is Rugby Union

explanation.surface: A furious spectator thinks rugby has become a form of punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a noun and the definition describes it: a thing used for punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A ferule is a flat ruler or cane once used to strike pupils' hands at school.

clue.text: After taunting Eton, I received good kicking

indicators.note: I received good puts the letter for good after the mixed letters
taunting needles and stirs up, so the letters of these two words are mixed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A schoolboy who mocked Eton got a well-deserved kicking.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is the famous English boarding school; here it is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To toe a ball is to kick it with the tip of the foot, so toeing is kicking.

clue.text: English tax firm returns set of 8

indicators.note: returns sends the pieces back the way they came, read from the end

parts.note: VAT is value added tax, the UK sales tax
CO is short for company

explanation.surface: An English tax firm filing returns, with eight on file.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returns' looks like tax returns, but it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An octave is a group of eight, such as eight notes of a scale or eight lines of a sonnet.
